structured_output.world_model:
W5 (contrarian), after E049. The tip is E049: 5.198 s, 0.7535. It is E036 plus a group-2 freeze from 90% (annealed over 75–90%) plus a +0.25 true-epoch top-up. That is 9.5 epochs, ceil(9.5×25) = 238 steps, and the 10th loop runs only 13 steps.

1. Noise. The same commit (60645dd) read 0.7532, 0.7525, 0.7497 and 0.7544 on seeds 0–2 across rebuilds: SD about 0.2 pp around a population mean of about 0.7527. A neutral change clears 0.753 about 45% of the time. Bands for neutral changes should be ±0.3 pp. Time reproduces to about ±0.03 s. I missed E038 and E043 on accuracy because I underestimated the rebuild spread. A deterministic build (I079) is the most valuable infrastructure left. My guess is that the cuDNN wgrad picked by benchmark=True plus autotune reselection drives most of the spread.

2. From the code: muon_update applies no wd and renormalizes filters to √C_out every step. Filter wd is inert, so every wd result acts only through the SGD groups (BN biases at 64× lr, whitening bias, head). The optimum is near ×0.5.

3. Freezing with an annealed LR is close to free once the block has seen enough 32 px training (E028, E036, E046, E049). An early freeze is not (E037 at 60%). Each frozen block saves 1.5–2× its FLOP share, because it also skips its BN/GELU backward, its Muon NS and the next group's dgrad (E046: about 10 ms per frozen step, a surprise to everyone). The cascade plus top-up beat the dial (E049 kept). Extending the freeze dose follows the same pattern as E037: the anneal start moves earlier and costs accuracy roughly linearly.

4. Steps carry accuracy and early pixels don't (E026, E033 free; E040, E041, E031, E048 cost about the dial rate; E045 bought at about the dial rate). The dial is about 1.2–1.8 s/pp. Loss-based selection is roughly dial-equivalent, so stacking it with a top-up nets about zero.

5. Changing the objective or the averaging costs 0.2–0.5 pp (E025, E030, E032, E044). Architecture changes that cut spatial work in the stem (a strided conv instead of conv+maxpool) remove the max-pool's translation invariance and three-quarters of conv1's positions. airbench ablations found conv+pool beats a strided conv by about 0.5–1 pp at short budgets. I expect a large saving (the 31×31 tensor is the biggest memory-bound one) but a worse s/pp than the dial. ReLU over GELU is a similar trade: about 2–3% time for an expected 0.2–0.4 pp.

6. Hidden systems waste remains. Every epoch loop augments, interpolates and permutes all 50k images at each resolution it touches, including the 13-step final loop. On top of that, cudagraph copy-in costs about 1%. Making these lazy is identical math worth about 1–2%. This is the safest remaining gain.

7. The PCIe judge adds about 5–10% to absolute times. The ranking mostly holds, and bandwidth-bound savings shrink slightly.

Unsure:
- whether within-build runs are bit-identical (atomics in wgrad);
- whether Inductor saves a mask for ReLU;
- the size of the strided-conv accuracy loss on CIFAR-100;
- whether seeds 13–32 are harder or the gap is winner's curse.

forecasts.reason: Identical math removes about 60–100 ms of copy/interpolate/augmentation waste. Accuracy is the same, up to rebuild noise.
Fused BN/act kernels are mostly bytes-bound, so the saving is about 2–3% (below 3%). ReLU likely costs about 0.2–0.4 pp on CIFAR-100.
Diagnostic on the E036 commit. Within-build identity is plausible, but rebuild identity is uncertain without pinning, and no-cudagraphs probably costs more than 0.5%.
Big stem saving, but dropping the max-pool's invariance and 3/4 of conv1's positions costs about 0.5–1 pp, which is worse than the dial's s/pp.
Selection is about dial-equivalent, so the net gain is about 0.05 s for about −0.05 pp, which is below noise.
About 13 more frozen steps save about 0.13 s, but the earlier group-2 anneal (from 70%) likely costs about 0.1–0.2 pp, which sits at the threshold.

cruxes: Can a pinned or deterministic build remove the ~0.2 pp rebuild spread on seeds 0–2? If it can, sub-0.15 pp levers such as I081/I082 become decidable; if not, only levers worth more than 0.3 pp or time-only changes can be judged.
How much does a stride-2 conv instead of conv+maxpool in group 1 cost on CIFAR-100? Under 0.3 pp would make I080 the biggest remaining lever (about 6–8%); over 0.5 pp closes stem-architecture cuts.
Is the fused BN/activation tail bytes-bound (ReLU saves under 2%) or erf-compute-sensitive (ReLU saves 3% or more)?
